newsitem.title: GERMANY: Transrapid seeks alliance with GEC-Alsthom.
newsitem.headline: Transrapid seeks alliance with GEC-Alsthom.

text.p: The newly-reorganised industry consortium planning Germany's Transrapid high-speed rail project is holding talks with Anglo-French group GEC Alsthom, Siemens chief executive Heinrich von Pierer said on Friday.
"We see good chances that these talks will end positively," von Pierer told a news conference in Bonn.

Siemens, together with Thyssen AG and the Deutsche Bahn railways, remains at the core of the Transrapid consortium after news of the planned withdrawal of the construction groups originally involved in the project.
GEC Alsthom, a joint venture between Britain's GEC and France's Alcatel Alsthom, was one of the firms responsible for creating France's TGV high-speed rail network.
Industry analysts have in the past said that broader European participation in Transrapid could help it be more easily integrated into broader European transport networks.
